subject: Post-call: model evaluation roadmap & acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Green <sophie.green@finly.com>, Rajiv Nair <rajiv@paycore.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: model evaluation roadmap & acceptance thresholds

Hi Sophie / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and a proposed roadmap so we can move from discovery to a runnable eval:

What we heard (summary)
- Primary goal: replace parts of your customer support triage and policy-checking pipeline with an LLM-driven assistant while maintaining near-zero false-positives on policy enforcement and keeping hallucinations below business-tolerable levels.
- Data: ~5k weekly interactions, mix of short intents + multi-turn follow-up clarifications, some PII/PCI elements (tokenized).
- Constraints: p95 latency target < 300ms for single-turn inference in prod; strict auditability and traceability.

Recommended quick model slate to test (open vs your proprietary baseline)
- Open candidates: Redwood-Open-7B-v2-qlora (cheap, fast), Llama-3-20B-quant (strong instruction-following), Mistral-Instruct-8x (good for classification).
- Customer baseline: FinlyProd-Baseline v1 (your in-house proprietary model; we treated this as the reference).

Suggested acceptance criteria (initial intent/quality thresholds)
- Intent accuracy (top-1) >= 97% on holdout test set
- Slot-filling F1 >= 0.94
- Hallucination incidents <= 1% (measured on a 1k sample with human labelers)
- Cost target: delta <= +20% vs baseline (we can tune quantization/batching if higher)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms in dedicated testing environment

Planned eval approach (2-week runnable plan)
1) Technical workshop (this week) — exchange schema & 5k anon sample, agree test splits.
2) Benchmarks: run held-out eval for the slate above (functional metrics + hallucination sampling + latency/cost).
3) Canary / shadow run (optional): 10% traffic for 48–72 hrs to compare live regressions.
4) Acceptance decision: compare against thresholds, then recommend rollout (A/B or progressive).

Attachments & links
- Attached: prospect-dd-notes.pdf (call notes), prompt-set-v1.jsonl (initial prompt templates), open-vs-prop-comparison.xlsx (evaluation matrix template).
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/finly-eval-promptsets
- Internal eval run: https://redwood.app/evals/D-2026-0934

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm whether the sample can be tokenized/anonymized for transfer?
- Any hard constraints on cost or quantization (e.g., cannot use 4-bit weights)?
- Are there regulatory constraints that require on-prem-only evaluation?

Next steps we propose
- Marcus to run a quick benchmark on the provided sample once we have it (ETA 3 business days).
- Schedule a 60-min technical workshop with your infra/ML folks — suggest Tue/Thu next week.

If this looks good I'll push the calendar invites and we can start dataset transfer.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0196

Subject: Re: Post-call: model evaluation roadmap & acceptance thresholds

Mina —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side before we kick off:

1) Data residency / compliance: Finly requires that production customer data never leave our VPC during any live canary. For the held-out eval, we can provide a tokenized & anonymized 5k sample — is that sufficient for initial benchmarking?

2) Hallucination definition: the 1% threshold is encouraging but can you outline how Redwood measures hallucinations? We need to ensure labelling methodology aligns with our internal reviewers.

3) Comparison to our baseline: the FinlyProd-Baseline v1 is tuned heavily for our taxonomy. Can your open-model slate be fine-tuned or prompt-tuned against a small labeled set (2–3k records) in your hosted eval, or would that need to happen on-prem?

4) Cost sensitivity: our legal/finance team has a soft cap on per-token inference of ~$0.04 equivalent. If the open model ends up costing more than our baseline, we need a clear plan for cost mitigation before any production rollout.

If you can answer these points and confirm a proposed workshop time (Tue 10–11am ET or Thu 2–3pm ET both work), we can move the sample over and loop in our infra lead.

— Sophie
Sophie Green
Director, Automation & Customer Experience
Finly Payments
sophie.green@finly.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Green <sophie.green@finly.com>, Rajiv Nair <rajiv@paycore.io>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evaluation roadmap & acceptance thresholds

Hi Sophie — thanks for the questions, I’ll address each and outline how we propose to measure things so results are auditable.

1) Data residency / on-prem constraint
- For any live canary we will run inside your VPC / Private deployment (Redwood Private) — no customer data leaves your network. For initial held-out benchmarking, tokenized/anonymized samples are sufficient to estimate intent accuracy and hallucination rate. If you prefer, we can also run the benchmark inside a customer-managed Private deployment (we have a lightweight runner we can deploy).

2) Hallucination measurement method
- We use a two-stage approach: automated filters (NER overlap, factual-check heuristics) + human adjudication on a sampled 1k subset. Metrics reported: hallucination_rate (boolean per-response) and severity buckets (minor/major). We'll share the adjudication rubric ahead of time so your reviewers can align.

3) Fine-tuning / prompt-tuning options
- Options:
  a) Prompt-tuning only (fast): we run prompt/adapter tuning on your labeled 2–3k set using a small adapter layer — can be done in hosted eval or in your VPC if required.
  b) Parameter fine-tuning: recommended only if prompt-tuning doesn't reach thresholds; this requires more compute and (for your comfort) we can run it inside the Private deployment.

4) Cost mitigation levers
- Quantization (4-bit), dynamic batching, and prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts typically cut per-token cost by 30–60%. We'll provide a cost sensitivity matrix after an initial pass; if the open candidate still exceeds your cap we can recommend a smaller model or rely on the proprietary baseline with hybrid routing for high-risk flows.

Proposed technical experiment (concrete)
- Dataset: your anonymized 5k sample (split 70/15/15) + 1k human-labeled hallucination sample.
- Runs: Redwood-Open-7B-v2-qlora (prompt-tuned), Llama-3-20B-quant (no-tune baseline), FinlyProd-Baseline v1 (you supply eval outputs or we run shadowed comparisons).
- Metrics: intent_acc, slot_F1, hallucination_rate, p95_latency (dedicated env), cost_estimated_per_1k_tokens.
- Canary plan (if benchmarks pass): 10% traffic for 48h with rollback triggers: +1% drop in intent_acc or >2x hallucination rate vs baseline.

Links & artifacts
- Eval matrix template attached: open-vs-prop-comparison.xlsx
- Prompt set (initial): https://drive.google.com/finly-eval-promptsets

If you approve, we’ll:
1) get the anonymized sample (SFTP or secure Drive link)
2) run the first-pass benchmarks (ETA 72 hrs after data receipt)
3) share a short report + recommended next action (tune / canary / stop).

Regards,

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
